source_document: Document 12 — Washington to Madison, November 5, 1786 (11.2 Casefile B)
source_text: What stronger evidence can be given of the weakness of our governments than these disorders? If no power exists to check them, what security has a man of life, liberty, or property? Thirteen sovereignties pulling against each other, and all tugging at the federal head, will soon bring ruin on the whole.
prompt: Write 2–3 sentences of historical context for this letter.
sentence_starter: In the late summer and fall of 1786, ___
checklist: Did you name when and where?
Did you name what was happening at the time?
Did you connect it to why the letter matters?
model_response: In the late summer and fall of 1786, the United States was governed by the Articles of Confederation, and armed farmers in Massachusetts were shutting down courts to stop the seizure of their farms. Congress had no money and could not pay for an army to respond, which is why Washington, writing privately to Madison, feared the country was heading toward ruin.
